notes:
Copilot `!` shell escape. KNOWN FAILING against the adapter as committed. LIVE on CLI 1.0.77 the escape runs locally with no model turn (footer stayed at 'Session: 0 AIC used') and appends exactly two lines to events.jsonl — {"type":"tool.user_requested","data":{"toolName":"local_shell","arguments":{"command":"echo third"}}} and {"type":"tool.execution_complete","data":{"isUserRequested":true,"success":true,"result":{…}}} — with NO assistant.turn_end. The copilot parser skips tool.user_requested (unknown type → default Skip) but maps tool.execution_complete → function_call_output (parser.go:102-103,224-232), which is substantive activity: forceReadyToWorkingIfActive bounces ready→working (session_detector_activity.go:582) and IsAgentDone is false for function_call_output (metrics.go:513-558), so the session STICKS in working. This spec asserts the CORRECT behaviour per the intent reading adopted by the claudecode and mistral-vibe siblings — state stays ready across the escape window, exactly as vibe's injected:true skip (vibe/parser.go:127-136) and claudecode's <bash-input>/<bash-stdout> skip (claudecode/parser.go:350-359) guarantee for those adapters. UNLOCK: skip tool.execution_complete when data.isUserRequested == true; model-invoked completions (no such field, paired with tool.execution_start) are untouched. ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: a real turn runs FIRST because copilot's event writer batches — on a fresh session two escapes wrote NO events.jsonl for ~50 s, and the buffered events were flushed only when the first prompt created the file, landing BEFORE its user.message where the trailing turn_end masks the defect. Once the file exists, an escape appends within 5 s. A claudecode-order recipe (escape first) would record GREEN over a broken adapter. PRESESSION SHAPE: session-state/<id>/ is created at launch holding only workspace.yaml and sessionIDFromPath claims only events.jsonl, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a proc-<PID> row before the fswatcher sees any transcript and the real session arrives under a DIFFERENT id — birth is two phases, every later phase anchored to the real session. OBSERVATIONS: two real turns, so tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map. model is NOT pinned — --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn.

KNOWN_FAILING CLEARED 2026-08-05 (CLI 1.0.78) — BY A RE-RECORDING, NOT A SPEC REBASE. The bug was real when frozen: the `!` escape runs a command LOCALLY with no model turn (the CLI's own credit counter stays at zero) but still appends tool.user_requested + tool.execution_complete{isUserRequested:true} to events.jsonl, and crucially emits NO assistant.turn_end. Mapping that completion to function_call_output bounced a settled session ready → working with nothing left to ever close it, so the session stuck in working for the rest of its life — the identical shape mistral-vibe hit with its own `!` escape. The parser now Skips both records, pinned red-first by TestShellEscapeDoesNotStickWorking. This recording is the live proof: tool.user_requested (local_shell) lands at 15:36:41.913 and its completion at 15:36:42.005, and the daemon emits NO transition of any kind between the first turn settling at 17:36:35.423 and the next real prompt at 17:36:53.348 — 17.9 seconds of preserved `ready` spanning the whole escape.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)

The first real prompt materializes events.jsonl, so the real <session-id> session reconciles under a different id and is born DIRECTLY into working (commit 3cde4f8d) — the session row exists and is real BEFORE the shell escape fires
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
assistant.turn_end settles the first turn back to ready — the state the escape window must preserve

After `!echo hello` runs locally, state stays ready: the escape is not a turn, so no state change may be synthesized from its tool.user_requested / tool.execution_complete pair. FAILS TODAY — tool.execution_complete maps to function_call_output, flipping the session to working with no turn_done to close it, so it sticks there until the next real prompt. That stick is exactly what this scenario exists to catch.
After the escape window, a normal user prompt drives ready → working — proves the session is still alive and not wedged
